title.zh: 卷八十五 晉書11: 少帝本紀五
title.en: Volume 85 Book of Later Jin 11: Emperor Shao 4
title.raw: 卷八十五 晉書11: 少帝本紀五 Volume 85 Book of Later Jin 11: Emperor Shao 4

sentences.zh: 開運三年冬十月甲子，正衙命使冊皇太妃安氏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyun, winter, tenth month, on jiazi day, edict messengers from the main court were charged to invest Grand Consort An.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi in the tenth month of winter in Kaiyun's third year, envoys from the main court were sent to invest Grand Consort Lady An.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以樞密直學士、禮部侍郎邊光範為翰林學士，以給事中邊歸讜為左散騎常侍，以翰林學士、祠部員外郎、知制誥張沆為右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: On jichou day, Bian Guangfan, Academician Direct of the Bureau of Military Affairs and Vice Minister of Rites, was made Hanlin Academician; Bian Guichan, Supervising Secretary, was made Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry; Zhang Hong, Hanlin Academician, Vice Director of the Sacrificial Ceremonies Office, and Drafter of Imperial Edicts, was made Right Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Bian Guangfan—direct academician of the Bureau of Military Affairs and vice minister of rites—was appointed Hanlin academician; supervising secretary Bian Guichan became left regular attendant of the cavalry; and Hanlin academician Zhang Hong, who also served as vice director of sacrificial ceremonies and drafter of edicts, became right remonstrating grand master.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以鄴都留守杜威為北面行營都招討使，以侍衛親軍都指揮使、鄆州節度使李守貞為兵馬都監，兗州安審琦為左右廂都指揮使，徐州符彥卿為馬軍左廂都指揮使，滑州皇甫遇為馬軍右廂都指揮使，貝州梁漢璋為馬軍都排陣使，前鄧州宋彥筠為步軍左廂都指揮使，奉國左廂都指揮使王饒為步軍右廂都指揮使，洺州團練使薛懷讓為先鋒都指揮使。

translations.literal: On xinwei day, Du Wei, military governor of Ye, was made Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Expeditionary Headquarters; Li Shouzhen, commander-in-chief of the Imperial Guard and military governor of Yan Prefecture, was made overseer of troops and horses; An Shenqi of Yanzhou was made commander of the left and right wings; Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou was made commander of the left wing of the horse army; Huangfu Yu of Hua Prefecture was made commander of the right wing of the horse army; Liang Hanzhang of Bei Prefecture was made marshal of the horse army's battle array; Song Yanjun, former prefect of Deng, was made commander of the left wing of the foot army; Wang Rao, commander of the left wing of the Fengguo Army, was made commander of the right wing of the foot army; and Xue Huairang, training commissioner of Ming Prefecture, was made vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Ye's military governor Du Wei was named overall commander of the northern expedition; Li Shouzhen, commander of the imperial guard and governor of Yanzhou, became overseer of troops and horses; An Shenqi of Yanzhou took the left and right wings; Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou led the horse army's left wing; Huangfu Yu of Huazhou the right wing; Liang Hanzhang of Beizhou marshaled the horse array; former Dengzhou prefect Song Yanjun the foot army's left wing; Fengguo left-wing commander Wang Rao the foot right wing; and Mingzhou training commissioner Xue Huairang the vanguard.

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （案：《通鑒》載，當時敕榜曰：「先取瀛、鄚，安定關南；

translations.literal: (According to the Zizhi Tongjian, the edict placard of the time read: "First take Ying and Mo and secure the lands south of the pass;
translations.idiomatic: (The Zizhi Tongjian records that the campaign edict proclaimed: "First seize Ying and Mo and pacify the territory south of the pass;

sentences.zh: 次復幽、燕，蕩平塞北。

translations.literal: next recover You and Yan and sweep the northern frontier flat."
translations.idiomatic: then recover You and Yan and pacify the northern marches."

sentences.zh: 」蓋狃於陽城之役而驟驕也。）〉

translations.literal: This was because they clung to the victory at Yangcheng and suddenly grew arrogant.)〉
translations.idiomatic: They had grown arrogant overnight on the strength of Yangcheng.)〉

sentences.zh: 癸酉，冊吳國夫人馮氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On guiyou day, Lady Feng, consort of the State of Wu, was invested as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Wu State consort Lady Feng was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以侍衛馬軍都指揮使李彥韜權知侍衛司事。

translations.literal: On yihai day, Li Yantao, commander-in-chief of the imperial horse guard, was made acting superintendent of the Imperial Guard Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, imperial horse-guard commander Li Yantao was placed in acting charge of the imperial guard bureau.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，鳳翔節度使秦王李從嚴薨，輟朝，冊贈尚書令。

translations.literal: On bingxu day, Li Congyan, Prince of Qin and military governor of Fengxiang, died; court audiences were suspended, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Prince of Qin Li Congyan, military governor of Fengxiang, died; the court mourned and posthumously enfeoffed him minister of works.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，邠州節度使李德充卒，輟朝，贈太尉。

translations.literal: On dinghai day, Li Dechong, military governor of Bin Prefecture, died; court audiences were suspended, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Binzhou governor Li Dechong died; audiences were suspended and he was posthumously made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊子朔，以給事中盧撰為右散騎常侍，以尚書兵部郎中兼侍御史、知雜事陳觀為左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month, wuzi, Lu Zhuan, Supervising Secretary, was made Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and Chen Guan, Director of the Bureau of Personnel in the Ministry of War and concurrent Supervising Censor and chief of miscellaneous matters, was made Left Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the first of the eleventh month, supervising secretary Lu Zhuan became right regular cavalry attendant, and Chen Guan, director in the war ministry with concurrent censor duties, became left remonstrating grand master.

sentences.zh: 觀以祖諱「義」，乞改官，尋授給事中。

translations.literal: Because his grandfather's name was "Yi," Guan requested a change of office and was soon appointed Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Guan asked for a new post because his grandfather's name was Yi; he was soon made supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，樞密使、中書侍郎兼戶部尚書、平章事馮玉加尚書右僕射，以皇子鎮寧軍節度使延煦為陜州節度使，以陜州留後焦繼勛為鳳翔留後，以前定州留後安審琦為邠州留後，以右僕射和凝為左僕射。

translations.literal: On gengyin day, Feng Yu, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Concurrent Minister of Revenue and Grand Councilor, was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right; the Prince's military governor of Zhenning Army, Yanshu, was made military governor of Shan Prefecture; Jiao Jixun, acting governor of Shan, was made acting governor of Fengxiang; An Shenqi, former acting governor of Ding, was made acting governor of Bin; and He Ning, Vice Minister of the Right, was made Vice Minister of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, grand councilor Feng Yu, bureau commissioner and vice minister of the secretariat with concurrent revenue portfolio, was promoted right vice minister; Prince Yanshu, governor of Zhenning, took Shanzhou; Shan acting governor Jiao Jixun became Fengxiang acting governor; former Ding acting governor An Shenqi took Bin; and right vice minister He Ning moved to the left.

sentences.zh: 甲午，兩浙節度使吳越國王錢宏佐起復舊任。

translations.literal: On jiawu day, Qian Hongzuo, military governor of the Two Zhes and king of Wuyue, resumed his former duties after mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Wuyue king and Two-Zhe governor Qian Hongzuo returned from mourning to his old post.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔李守貞知幽州行府事。

translations.literal: On dingyou day, an edict made Li Shouzhen acting administrator of the Youzhou field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Li Shouzhen was ordered to administer the Youzhou field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 戊申，日南至，禦崇元殿受朝賀。

translations.literal: On wushen day, the winter solstice; the Emperor attended audience and received congratulations in the Chongyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, the winter solstice, the emperor received New Year congratulations in the Chongyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 是月，北面行營招討使杜威率諸將領大軍自鄴北征，師次瀛州城下，貝州節度使梁漢璋戰死。

translations.literal: That month, Du Wei, Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Expeditionary Headquarters, led the generals and the main army north from Ye; when the army reached below Ying Prefecture city, Liang Hanzhang, military governor of Bei Prefecture, died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: That month Du Wei led the main northern army out of Ye; below Yingzhou city, Beizhou governor Liang Hanzhang was killed in action.

sentences.zh: 杜威等以漢璋之敗，遂收軍而退。

translations.literal: Because of Hanzhang's defeat, Du Wei and the others withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: After Hanzhang's defeat, Du Wei pulled the army back.

sentences.zh: 行次武強，聞契丹入寇，欲取直路，自冀、貝而南。

translations.literal: When they reached Wuqiang, they heard that the Khitan had invaded and wished to take a direct route south through Ji and Bei.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuqiang they learned the Khitan had invaded and meant to strike south through Ji and Bei by the shortest road.

sentences.zh: 會張彥澤領騎自鎮定至，且言契丹可破之狀，於是大軍西趨鎮州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yanzhe arrived leading cavalry from Zhen and Ding and also said the Khitan could be broken, the main army then hurried west toward Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yanzhe came from Zhending with cavalry, insisting the Khitan could be crushed, and the main force turned west for Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁巳朔，

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month, dingsi,
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, the first day of the twelfth month,

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （案：以下有闕文。

translations.literal: (According to the Zizhi Tongjian: the text below is defective.
translations.idiomatic: (The Zizhi Tongjian notes lacunae below.

sentences.zh: 據《通鑒》云：丁巳朔，李穀自書密奏，且言大軍危急之勢，請車駕幸滑州，遣高行周、符彥卿扈從，及發兵守澶州、河陽，以備敵之奔沖。

translations.literal: According to the Zizhi Tongjian: on dingsi, the first day, Li Gu wrote a secret memorial from his own hand, stating moreover the army's grave peril and asking that the imperial carriage proceed to Hua Prefecture, with Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing as escorts, and that troops be sent to hold Cang and Heyang against the enemy's rush south.
translations.idiomatic: It adds that on that dingsi new moon Li Gu penned a secret memorial describing the army's peril, urging the emperor to move to Huazhou with Gao Xingzhou and Fu Yanqing as escort, and to garrison Cangzhou and Heyang against a Khitan dash south.

sentences.zh: 遣軍將關勛走馬上之。）〉

translations.literal: He dispatched the officer Guan Xun to gallop and deliver it on horseback.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He sent officer Guan Xun to ride ahead with the dispatch.)〉

sentences.zh: 己未，杜威奏，駐軍於中渡橋。

translations.literal: On jiwei day, Du Wei memorialized that the army was encamped at the Zhongdu Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Du Wei reported the army encamped at Zhongdu Bridge.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以前司農卿儲延英為太子賓客。

translations.literal: On gengshen day, Chu Yanying, former Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, former agriculture director Chu Yanying became mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 詔徐州符彥卿屯澶州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou to garrison Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yanqing of Xuzhou was ordered to hold Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，詔澤潞、鄴都、邢洺、河陽運糧赴中渡，杜威遣人口奏軍前事宜，勢迫故也。

translations.literal: On xinyou day, an edict ordered Ze-Lu, Ye, Xing-Ming, and Heyang to transport grain to Zhongdu; Du Wei sent men to report matters at the front orally because the situation was pressing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Ze-Lu, Ye, Xing-Ming, and Heyang were told to ship grain to Zhongdu; Du Wei sent oral reports from the front under pressure.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，又遣高行周屯澶州，景延廣守河陽。

translations.literal: On renxu day, Gao Xingzhou was again sent to garrison Cang, and Jing Yanguang to hold Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Gao Xingzhou was again posted to Cangzhou and Jing Yanguang to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 博野縣都監張鵬入奏蕃軍事勢。

translations.literal: Zhang Peng, chief inspector of Boye County, entered court to report the Khitan army's strength.
translations.idiomatic: Boye county inspector Zhang Peng came in to report Khitan strength.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，定州李殷奏，前月二十八日夜，領捉生四百人往曲陽嘉山下，逢敵軍車帳，殺千餘人，獲馬二百匹。

translations.literal: On bingyin day, Li Yin of Ding Prefecture memorialized that on the night of the twenty-eighth of the previous month he had led four hundred scouts to the foot of Jia Mountain in Quyang, encountered enemy wagons and tents, killed more than a thousand men, and captured two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Dingzhou's Li Yin reported that on the previous month's twenty-eighth he led four hundred scouts to Jia Mountain below Quyang, struck enemy camp trains, killed over a thousand, and took two hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 詔宋州高行周充北面行營都部署，符彥卿充副，邢州方太充都虞候，領後軍駐於河上，以備敵騎之奔沖也。

translations.literal: An edict made Gao Xingzhou of Song Prefecture overall commander of the northern expeditionary headquarters, Fu Yanqing deputy, Fang Tai of Xing Prefecture chief of staff, to lead the rear army garrisoned on the river against the enemy cavalry's rush south.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xingzhou of Songzhou was named northern commander, Fu Yanqing his deputy, and Xingzhou's Fang Tai chief of staff, to hold the rear on the river against Khitan cavalry breaking south.

sentences.zh: 時契丹遊騎涉滹水而南，至欒城縣。

translations.literal: At that time Khitan raiders crossed the Hutuo River southward as far as Luancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan raiders then forded the Hutuo south to Luancheng.

sentences.zh: 自是中渡寨為蕃軍隔絕，探報不通，朝廷大恐，故委行周等繼領兵師守扼津要，且以張其勢也。

translations.literal: From then on the Zhongdu stockade was cut off by the Khitan army; scouts could not get through, and the court was greatly alarmed; therefore Xingzhou and the others were entrusted to continue leading troops to hold the fords and passes and also to display their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdu camp was now cut off and no scouts got through; the court in panic sent Xingzhou and others to hold the crossings and show force.

sentences.zh: 己巳，邢州方太奏，此月六日，契丹與王師戰於中渡，王師不利，奉國都指揮使王清戰死。

translations.literal: On jisi day, Fang Tai of Xing Prefecture memorialized that on the sixth of this month the Khitan and the imperial army fought at Zhongdu; the imperial army was unfavorable, and Wang Qing, commander-in-chief of the Fengguo Army, died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Xingzhou's Fang Tai reported that on the sixth the Khitan beat the imperial force at Zhongdu; Fengguo commander Wang Qing fell.

sentences.zh: 庚午，幸沙臺射兔。

translations.literal: On gengwu day, the Emperor went to Shatai to shoot hares.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu the emperor hunted hares at Shatai.

sentences.zh: 壬申，始聞杜威、李守貞等以此月十日率諸軍降於契丹。

translations.literal: On renshen day, it was first learned that on the tenth of this month Du Wei, Li Shouzhen, and the others had led the armies to surrender to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen came first word that on the tenth Du Wei and Li Shouzhen had surrendered the army to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 是夜，相州節度使張彥澤受契丹命，率先鋒二千人，自封丘門斬關而入。

translations.literal: That night, Zhang Yanzhe, military governor of Xiang Prefecture, obeying the Khitan command, led two thousand vanguard troops to cut through the Fengqiu Gate and enter.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xiangzhou governor Zhang Yanzhe, under Khitan orders, led two thousand vanguard troops through Fengqiu Gate.

sentences.zh: 癸酉旦，張彥澤頓兵於明德門外，京城大擾。

translations.literal: At dawn on guiyou day, Zhang Yanzhe stationed troops outside the Gate of Virtue Manifest; the capital was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on guiyou, Zhang Yanzhe halted outside Virtue Gate and the capital erupted.

sentences.zh: 前曹州節度使石赟死，帝之堂叔也。

translations.literal: Shi Yun, former military governor of Cao Prefecture, died; he was the Emperor's paternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Former Caozhou governor Shi Yun died—the emperor's uncle.

sentences.zh: 時自中渡寨隔絕之後，帝與大臣端坐憂危，國之衛兵，悉在北面，計無所出。

translations.literal: From the time the Zhongdu stockade was cut off, the Emperor and the great ministers sat upright in peril; the state's guards were all on the northern front, and no plan could be found.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhongdu was isolated the emperor and ministers sat trapped while every guardsman was north and no plan availed.

sentences.zh: 十六日聞滹水之降。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth it was learned of the surrender at the Hutuo.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth came news of surrender at the Hutuo.

sentences.zh: 是夜，偵知張彥澤已至滑州，召李崧、馮玉、李彥韜入內計事，方議詔河東劉知遠起兵赴難，至五鼓初，張彥澤引蕃騎入京。

translations.literal: That night, learning that Zhang Yanzhe had already reached Hua Prefecture, Li Song, Feng Yu, and Li Yantao were summoned within to plan; they were just discussing an edict for Liu Zhiyuan of Hedong to raise troops for rescue when, at the beginning of the fifth watch, Zhang Yanzhe led Khitan cavalry into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That night, told Zhang Yanzhe had reached Huazhou, Li Song, Feng Yu, and Li Yantao were called in; as they drafted orders for Hedong's Liu Zhiyuan to march, Zhang Yanzhe entered the capital with Khitan horse at fifth watch.

sentences.zh: 宮中相次火起，帝自攜劍驅擁后妃已下十數人，將同赴火，為親校薛超所持。

translations.literal: Fires broke out one after another in the palace; the Emperor himself took a sword and drove the empress and more than ten others below her, intending to enter the fire together, but was seized by his intimate guard Xue Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Palace fires broke out in succession; the emperor drew his sword to drive the empress and a dozen kin toward the flames, but intimate guard Xue Chao seized him.

sentences.zh: 俄自寬仁門遞入契丹主與皇太后書，帝乃止，旋令撲滅煙火。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter a letter from the Khitan ruler and the empress dowager was passed in through the Gate of Broad Benevolence; the Emperor then stopped and at once ordered the fires extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a letter from the Khitan ruler and empress dowager came through Broad Benevolence Gate; the emperor halted and ordered the fires put out.

sentences.zh: 大內都點檢康福全在寬仁門宿衛，登樓覘賊，彥澤呼而下之。

translations.literal: Kang Quanquan, chief inspector of the inner palace, was on guard at the Gate of Broad Benevolence; he climbed the tower to spy on the bandits; Yanzhe called him down.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-palace inspector Kang Quanquan guarded Broad Benevolence Gate, climbed the tower to watch the raiders, and Yanzhe summoned him down.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，帝奉表於戎主曰：

translations.literal: On guiyou day, the Emperor presented a memorial to the Khitan ruler, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the emperor submitted this memorial to the Khitan ruler:

sentences.zh: 孫臣某言：今月十七日寅時，相州節度使張彥澤、都監傅住兒部領大軍入京，賫到翁皇帝賜太后書示，於滹沱河降下杜重威一行馬步兵士，見領蕃漢步騎來幸汴州者。

translations.literal: Grandson and subject so-and-so states: on the seventeenth of this month at the yin hour, Xiang Prefecture military governor Zhang Yanzhe and overseer Fu Zhu'er led the main army into the capital, bearing the venerable emperor's letter to the empress dowager, showing that below the Hutuo Du Chongwei's line of horse and foot soldiers had surrendered and that the Khitan and Han foot and horse they now led were coming to Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Your grandson and subject writes: at yin on the seventeenth, Xiangzhou governor Zhang Yanzhe and overseer Fu Zhu'er entered the capital with the main force, bearing the Khitan emperor's letter to the empress dowager, announcing Du Chongwei's surrender at the Hutuo and that the mixed Khitan-Han host was marching on Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 往者，唐運告終，中原失馭，數窮否極，天缺地傾。

translations.literal: In the past the fortune of Tang had reached its end; the Central Plains lost their ruler; number exhausted and extremity reached, heaven cracked and earth tilted.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang's mandate ended the heartland was left masterless—fortune spent, heaven cracked, earth askew.

sentences.zh: 先人有田一成，有眾一旅，兵連禍結，力屈勢孤。

translations.literal: My forebear had one patch of field and one company of men; soldiers linked with calamity, strength bent and situation isolated.
translations.idiomatic: My forebear held a single field and a single company; war chained to disaster until strength failed and he stood alone.

sentences.zh: 翁皇帝救患摧鋒，興利除害，躬擐甲胄，深入寇場。

translations.literal: The venerable emperor rescued the afflicted and crushed the sharp edge, raised benefit and removed harm, personally donned armor, and deeply entered the bandit ground.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor relieved the suffering, crushed our foes, bore armor himself, and drove deep into enemy country.

sentences.zh: 犯露蒙霜，度雁門之險；

translations.literal: Braving dew and enduring frost, he crossed the peril of Yanmen;
translations.idiomatic: Through dew and frost he crossed Yanmen's passes;

sentences.zh: 馳風掣電，行中冀之誅。

translations.literal: wind racing and lightning pulling, he executed punishment in central Ji.
translations.idiomatic: With wind and lightning at his heels, he punished central Ji.

sentences.zh: 黃鉞一麾，天下大定。

translations.literal: With the yellow battle-axe waved once, the realm was greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: One wave of the battle-axe and the realm was settled.

sentences.zh: 勢淩宇宙，義感神明，功成不居，遂興晉祚，則翁皇帝有大造於石氏也。

translations.literal: His momentum overawed the cosmos; his righteousness moved the spirits; merit achieved he did not occupy it and instead raised the Jin mandate—thus the venerable emperor had great merit toward the House of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: His might overawed heaven; his righteousness moved the gods; refusing merit he enthroned Jin—so the Khitan emperor was founder to our house.

sentences.zh: 旋屬天降鞠兇，先君即世，臣遵承遺旨，纘紹前基。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter heaven sent down grievous misfortune; my late father passed away; your subject followed the testament and continued the former foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon heaven sent calamity; my father died; I followed his will and kept the throne.

sentences.zh: 諒暗之初，荒迷失次，凡有軍國重事，皆委將相大臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of mourning I was lost and out of step; all weighty matters of army and state were entrusted to the generals and great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In first mourning I was lost; every weight of army and state went to generals and ministers.

sentences.zh: 至於擅繼宗祧，既非稟命；

translations.literal: As for seizing succession to the ancestral temple on my own, it was not by command received;
translations.idiomatic: Seizing the temple succession was never commanded;

sentences.zh: 輕發文字，輒敢抗尊。

translations.literal: lightly issuing documents I dared resist the honored.
translations.idiomatic: I lightly issued edicts and dared defy your majesty.

sentences.zh: 自啟釁端，果貽赫怒，禍至神惑，運盡天亡。

translations.literal: Having myself opened the cause of strife, disaster indeed came—spirits confused, fortune exhausted, heaven perished.
translations.idiomatic: I opened the quarrel myself; wrath followed—spirits confused, fortune spent, heaven's favor gone.

sentences.zh: 十萬師徒，皆望風而束手；

translations.literal: A hundred thousand officers and soldiers all awaited the wind and bound their hands;
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand soldiers waited for the wind and bound their hands;

sentences.zh: 億兆黎庶，悉延頸以歸心。

translations.literal: hundreds of millions of common people all stretched their necks and turned their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: millions of people craned their necks in submission.

sentences.zh: 臣負義包羞，貪生忍恥，自貽顛覆，上累祖宗，偷度晨昏，茍存食息。

translations.literal: Your subject bore injustice wrapped in shame, clung to life enduring disgrace, brought down ruin on himself, and heaped it on ancestors, stealing through dawn and dusk, barely preserving breath.
translations.idiomatic: I bore shame, clung to life, ruined myself and shamed my ancestors, stealing breath from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 翁皇帝若惠顧疇昔，稍霽雷霆，未賜靈誅，不絕先祀，則百口荷更生之德，一門銜無報之恩，雖所願焉，非敢望也。

translations.literal: If the venerable emperor would look back on former days and slightly clear the thunder, not bestowing spirit punishment, not cutting off the former sacrifices, then a hundred mouths would bear the virtue of renewed life and one household would hold a debt that cannot be repaid—though this is what is wished, I do not dare to expect it.
translations.idiomatic: If you would recall old days, stay your thunder, spare my life and my ancestors' rites, a hundred mouths would owe rebirth and one house a debt beyond payment—this is my wish, though I dare not expect it.

sentences.zh: 臣與太后並妻馮氏及舉家戚屬，見於郊野面縛俟罪次。

translations.literal: Your subject, together with the empress dowager and consort Feng and the whole household of kin, now appear in the suburbs bound and awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: I, the empress dowager, consort Feng, and all our kin wait bound in the suburbs for judgment.

sentences.zh: 所有國寶一面、金印三面，今遣長子陜府節度使延煦、次子曹州節度使延寶管押進納，並奉表請罪，陳謝以聞。

translations.literal: There is one set of national treasures and three gold seals; your subject now sends the eldest son, military governor of Shan, Yanshu, and the second son, military governor of Cao, Yanbao, to escort and present them, and also presents this memorial requesting punishment, stating apology to inform.
translations.idiomatic: One imperial treasure set and three gold seals go forward under my eldest son Yanshu, Shanzhou governor, and second son Yanbao, Caozhou governor, with this plea for mercy.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，張彥澤遷帝與太后及諸宮屬於開封府，遣控鶴指揮使李榮將兵監守。

translations.literal: On jiaxu day, Zhang Yanzhe moved the Emperor, the empress dowager, and all palace kin to the office of the Kaifeng prefecture and sent Control-Crane commander Li Rong with troops to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Zhang Yanzhe moved the emperor, empress dowager, and palace kin to Kaifeng prefecture under Control-Crane commander Li Rong's guard.

sentences.zh: 是夜，開封尹桑維翰、宣徽使孟承誨皆遇害。

translations.literal: That night, Kaifeng prefect Sang Weihan and palace commissioner Meng Chenghui were both murdered.
translations.idiomatic: That night prefect Sang Weihan and palace commissioner Meng Chenghui were killed.

sentences.zh: 帝以契丹主將至，欲與太后出迎，彥澤先表之，稟契丹主之旨報云：「比欲許爾朝覲上國，臣僚奏言，豈有兩個天子道路相見！

translations.literal: Because the Khitan ruler was about to arrive, the Emperor wished to go out with the empress dowager to welcome him; Yanzhe reported first and, reporting the Khitan ruler's command, said: "We had intended to permit you to pay court in the superior state, but the ministers memorialized, saying how could two Sons of Heaven meet on the road!
translations.idiomatic: As the Khitan ruler approached, the emperor wished to go out with the empress dowager to welcome him; Yanzhe reported the Khitan reply: "We meant to let you attend court in our land, but ministers said two sons of heaven cannot meet on the road!

sentences.zh: 今賜所佩刀子，以慰爾心。

translations.literal: Now we bestow the knife you wear to comfort your heart."
translations.idiomatic: We now give the knife at your belt to comfort you."

sentences.zh: 」己卯，皇子延煦、延寶自帳中回，得敵詔慰撫，帝表謝之。

translations.literal: On jimao day, the princes Yanshu and Yanbao returned from the tent and received the enemy's edict of consolation; the Emperor presented a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, princes Yanshu and Yanbao returned from camp with the enemy's comforting edict; the emperor thanked them in memorial.

sentences.zh: 時契丹主以所送傳國寶制造非工，與載籍所述者異，使人來問。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan ruler, because the transmitted national treasure he had been sent was crudely made and differed from what the records described, sent a man to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler, finding the jade seal sent him poorly made and unlike the records, sent to inquire.

sentences.zh: 帝進狀曰：「頃以偽主王從珂於洛京大內自焚之後，其真傳國寶不知所在，必是當時焚之。

translations.literal: The Emperor submitted a statement saying: "Recently, after the false ruler Wang Congke burned himself in the great inner palace of Luoyang, the true transmitted treasure's whereabouts were unknown—it must have been burned at that time.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered: "After the false ruler Wang Congke burned himself in Luoyang's inner palace, the true seal vanished—surely it perished in that fire.

sentences.zh: 先帝受命，旋制此寶，在位臣僚，備知其事。

translations.literal: When my late father received the mandate he promptly fashioned this treasure; the ministers in office all know the matter.
translations.idiomatic: My father, taking the mandate, had this seal made; every minister in office knows it.

sentences.zh: 臣至今日，敢有隱藏」云。

translations.literal: Your subject to this day dares not conceal it," he said.
translations.idiomatic: To this day I dare not hide it," he wrote.

sentences.zh: 時移內庫至府，帝使人取帛數段，主者不與，謂使者曰：「此非我所有也。

translations.literal: When the inner storehouse was moved to the prefecture, the Emperor sent men to take several bolts of silk; the custodian would not give them, telling the envoy, "These are not mine."
translations.idiomatic: When the inner treasury moved to the prefecture, the emperor sent for silk; the keeper refused, saying, "These are not mine."

sentences.zh: 」又使人詣李崧求酒，崧曰：「臣有酒非敢愛惜，慮陛下杯酌之後憂躁，所作別有不測之事，臣以此不敢奉進。

translations.literal: The Emperor also sent men to Li Song to request wine; Song said, "Your subject has wine and does not dare be stingy, but fears that after Your Majesty's cup the worry and agitation might lead to other unforeseeable actions; your subject therefore does not dare present it."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked Li Song for wine; Song replied, "I have wine and do not begrudge it, but fear that after you drink, agitation may drive you to the unforeseen—I dare not offer it."

sentences.zh: 」丙戌晦，百官宿封禪寺。

translations.literal: On the last day of bingxu, the hundred officials lodged at the Fengchan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of bingxu the officials lodged at Fengchan Temple.

sentences.zh: 明年正月朔，契丹主次東京城北。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the next year, the Khitan ruler halted north of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the new year's first day the Khitan ruler halted north of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 百官列班，遙辭帝於寺，詣北郊以迎契丹主。

translations.literal: The hundred officials formed ranks, bade farewell to the Emperor from afar at the temple, and went to the northern suburbs to welcome the Khitan ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Officials lined up, bade the emperor farewell at the temple from afar, and went to the northern suburbs to welcome the Khitan ruler.

sentences.zh: 帝舉族出封丘門，肩轝至野，契丹主不與之見，遣泊封禪寺。

translations.literal: The Emperor and his whole clan went out the Fengqiu Gate, were carried on shoulder-poles to the wilds; the Khitan ruler did not meet them and sent them to lodge at the Fengchan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's clan went out Fengqiu Gate on litters to the open country; the Khitan ruler would not see them and sent them back to Fengchan Temple.

sentences.zh: 文武百官素服紗帽，迎謁契丹主於郊次，俯伏俟罪，契丹主命起之，親自慰撫。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials in plain white gauze caps welcomed and paid respects to the Khitan ruler at the suburban station, bowing prostrate and awaiting punishment; the Khitan ruler ordered them raised and personally consoled them.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials in white gauze caps met the Khitan ruler at the suburban station, prostrated themselves, and were raised and comforted by him.

sentences.zh: 契丹主遂入大內，至昏出宮，是夜宿於赤堈。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler then entered the great inner palace and at dusk left the palace; that night he lodged at Chijin.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler entered the inner palace and at dusk departed, lodging that night at Chijin.

sentences.zh: 偽詔應晉朝臣僚一切仍舊，朝廷儀制並用漢禮。

translations.literal: A false edict responded that all Jin dynasty ministers and officials should remain as before, and court ritual should all use Han rites.
translations.idiomatic: A puppet edict kept all Jin officials in post and retained Han court ritual.

sentences.zh: 戊子，殺鄭州防禦使楊承勛，責以背父之罪，令左右臠割而死。

translations.literal: On wuzi day, Yang Chengxun, defender of Zheng Prefecture, was killed, charged with the crime of betraying his father, and ordered cut to pieces by those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Zhengzhou defender Yang Chengxun was executed for betraying his father, hacked apart on the spot.

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《遼史》：以其弟承信為平盧軍節度使，襲父爵。）〉

translations.literal: (History of Liao: his younger brother Chenxin was made military governor of Pinglu Army and inherited his father's title.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (History of Liao: his brother Chenxin became Pinglu governor and inherited the father's rank.)〉

sentences.zh: 己丑，斬張彥澤於市，以其剽劫京城，恣行屠害也。

translations.literal: On jichou day, Zhang Yanzhe was beheaded in the market because he had plundered the capital and wantonly carried out slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Zhang Yanzhe was beheaded in the market for plundering the capital and massacring at will.

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《遼史》云：以張彥澤擅徙重貴開封，殺桑維翰，縱兵大掠，不道，斬於市。）〉

translations.literal: (History of Liao states: because Zhang Yanzhe had on his own moved Chonggui to Kaifeng, killed Sang Weihan, and let troops plunder greatly, for his unprincipled conduct he was beheaded in the market.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (History of Liao says Yanzhe was executed for moving Chonggui to Kaifeng, killing Sang Weihan, and letting troops loot the city.)〉

sentences.zh: 庚寅，洛京留守景延廣自扼吭而死。

translations.literal: On gengyin day, Jing Yanguang, acting governor of Luoyang, died by throttling himself.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Luoyang acting governor Jing Yanguang strangled himself.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，契丹制，降帝為光祿大夫、檢校太尉，封負義侯，黃龍府安置。

translations.literal: On xinmao day, by Khitan decree the Emperor was demoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Preceptor on inspection, enfeoffed as Marquis Who Bears Injustice, and settled at Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the Khitan demoted the emperor to grand master of splendid happiness and inspecting grand preceptor, enfeoffed him marquis who bears injustice, and sent him to Huanglong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其地在渤海國界。

translations.literal: That place lies on the border of the Bohai state.
translations.idiomatic: The place lay on Bohai's frontier.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，遷帝於封禪寺，遣蕃大將崔廷勛將兵守之。

translations.literal: On guisi day, the Emperor was moved to the Fengchan Temple, and the Khitan great general Cui Tingxun was sent with troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the emperor was moved to Fengchan Temple under Khitan general Cui Tingxun's guard.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，帝與皇太后李氏、皇太妃安氏、皇后馮氏、皇弟重睿、皇子延煦延寶俱北行，以宮嬪五十人、內官三十人、東西班五十人、醫官一人、控鶴官四人、禦廚七人、茶酒三人、儀鸞司三人、軍健二十人從行。

translations.literal: On guimao day, the Emperor, together with Empress Dowager Li, Grand Consort An, Empress Feng, his younger brother Chongrui, and the princes Yanshu and Yanbao, all traveled north, accompanied by fifty palace women, thirty inner attendants, fifty eastern and western class attendants, one medical officer, four control-crane officers, seven imperial cooks, three tea and wine officers, three ritual-standards officers, and twenty military attendants.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the emperor, Empress Dowager Li, Grand Consort An, Empress Feng, Prince Chongrui, and Yanshu and Yanbao marched north with fifty palace women, thirty eunuchs, fifty eastern and western attendants, and the usual train of doctors, cooks, and guards.

sentences.zh: 宰臣趙瑩、樞密使馮玉、侍衛馬軍都指揮使李彥韜隨帝入蕃，契丹主遣三百騎援送而去。

translations.literal: Chief minister Zhao Ying, Commissioner Feng Yu, and imperial horse-guard commander Li Yantao followed the Emperor into the Khitan lands; the Khitan ruler sent three hundred cavalry to escort them away.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Zhao Ying, commissioner Feng Yu, and horse-guard commander Li Yantao went into captivity with him; three hundred Khitan horsemen escorted them off.

sentences.zh: 所經州郡，長吏迎奉，皆為契丹主阻絕，有所供饋亦不通。

translations.literal: At every prefecture and commandery they passed, the chief officials came out to receive them, but all were blocked by the Khitan ruler; even what was offered for supply did not get through.
translations.idiomatic: At each prefecture local officials tried to receive them, but the Khitan ruler blocked every approach and even gifts could not pass.

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《宋史·李穀傳》：少帝蒙塵而北，舊臣無敢候謁者，穀獨拜迎於路，君臣相對泣下。

translations.literal: (History of Song, Biography of Li Gu: When the Minor Emperor suffered dust on the road north, none of the old ministers dared to wait and pay respects; only Gu alone bowed and received him on the road, ruler and minister facing each other weeping.)
translations.idiomatic: (History of Song, Biography of Li Gu: As the deposed emperor went north in disgrace, no former minister dared meet him—only Li Gu bowed to him on the road, and the two wept face to face.)

sentences.zh: 穀曰：「臣無狀，負陛下。

translations.literal: Gu said: "Your subject is without form, having failed Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "I am unworthy and have failed you."

sentences.zh: 」因傾囊以獻。）〉

translations.literal: He then emptied his purse and presented it.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Then he emptied his purse and offered what he had.)〉

sentences.zh: 嘗一日，帝與太后不能得食，乃殺畜而啖之。

translations.literal: Once on a certain day the Emperor and the empress dowager could not obtain food and so killed livestock and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion the emperor and empress dowager could get no food and slaughtered livestock to eat.

sentences.zh: 帝過中渡橋，閱前杜威營寨之跡，慨然憤嘆，謂左右曰：「我家何負，為此賊所破，天乎！

translations.literal: When the Emperor passed the Zhongdu Bridge and reviewed the traces of Du Wei's former encampment, he sighed in indignant lament and said to those at his side: "What have we done to deserve being ruined by this bandit? Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Crossing Zhongdu Bridge and seeing where Du Wei had camped, the emperor sighed in rage and told his attendants, "What did our house do to deserve ruin by this traitor? Heaven!

sentences.zh: 天乎！

translations.literal: Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: O Heaven!

sentences.zh: 」於是號慟而去。

translations.literal: Then he wailed and went on.
translations.idiomatic: He broke into loud wailing and went on.

sentences.zh: 至幽州，傾城士庶迎看於路，見帝慘沮，無不嗟嘆。

translations.literal: When he reached You Prefecture, the whole city's gentry and common people came out on the road to look; seeing the Emperor's wretched dejection, none failed to sigh.
translations.idiomatic: At Youzhou the whole city turned out along the road; seeing the emperor's misery, everyone sighed.

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《宣政雜錄》：徽宗北狩，經薊縣梁魚務，有還鄉橋，石少帝所命名也，里人至今呼之。）〉

translations.literal: (Miscellaneous Records of Xuanzheng: When Huizong went north on campaign, he passed Liangyu Post in Ji County; there was a Bridge of Return to the Homeland, named by the Minor Emperor of Shi, and the villagers to this day still call it by that name.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Miscellaneous Records of Xuanzheng: When Huizong was taken north, he passed Liangyu Post in Jixian, where the Later Jin minor emperor had named the Bridge of Return to the Homeland, which locals still use.)〉

sentences.zh: 駐留旬餘，州將承契丹命，犒帝於府署，趙延壽母以食饌來獻。

translations.literal: He remained more than ten days; the prefect, obeying Khitan orders, entertained the Emperor at the government office, and Zhao Yanshou's mother came to present food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: After a stay of ten-odd days, the prefect, on Khitan orders, feasted the emperor in his yamen, and Zhao Yanshou's mother brought food and drink.

sentences.zh: 自范陽行數十程，過薊州、平州，至榆關沙塞之地，略無供給，每至宿頓，無非路次，一行乏食，宮女、從官但采木實野蔬，以救饑弊。

translations.literal: From Fanyang they traveled several tens of stages, passing Ji Prefecture and Ping Prefecture to the sandy barrier at Yuguan; there was scarcely any supply; at every halt it was nothing but the roadside; the whole party lacked food, and palace women and attendant officials could only gather tree fruit and wild vegetables to relieve hunger.
translations.idiomatic: From Fanyang they marched dozens of stages through Jizhou and Pingzhou to Yuguan's desert barrier, with almost no supplies; at each halt they camped by the road, and the party starved while palace women and attendants gathered wild fruit and greens to survive.

sentences.zh: 又行七八日至錦州，契丹迫帝與妃後往拜安巴堅遺像，帝不勝屈辱，泣曰：「薛超誤我，不令我死，以至今日也。

translations.literal: After another seven or eight days they reached Jin Prefecture; the Khitan forced the Emperor and the consorts to go pay respects to the portrait of the deceased Anbajian; the Emperor could not bear the humiliation and wept, saying: "Xue Chao wronged me by not letting me die, so that it has come to this day."
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight days later at Jinzhou the Khitan forced the emperor and his consorts to bow before Anbajian's portrait; unable to bear the humiliation, he wept, "Xue Chao wronged me by keeping me alive until today."

sentences.zh: 」又行數十程，渡遼水，至黃龍府，即此所命安置之地也。

translations.literal: After several tens more stages they crossed the Liao River and reached Huanglong Prefecture—the very place appointed for their settlement.
translations.idiomatic: After many more stages they crossed the Liao River to Huanglong prefecture, the place of their exile.

sentences.zh: 六月，契丹國母召帝一行往懷密州，州在黃龍府西北千戎王裏。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Khitan empress dowager summoned the Emperor's party to go to Huaimi Prefecture, which lay a thousand li northwest of Huanglong Prefecture in the territory of the Thousand Rong Kings.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Khitan empress dowager summoned the party to Huaimi prefecture, a thousand li northwest of Huanglong in the Thousand Rong Kings' lands.

sentences.zh: 行至遼陽，皇后馮氏以帝陷蕃，過受艱苦，令內官潛求毒藥，將自飲之，並以進帝，不果而止。

translations.literal: When they reached Liaoyang, Empress Feng, because the Emperor had fallen into the Khitan lands and suffered excessive hardship, ordered an inner attendant secretly to seek poison, intending to drink it herself and also present it to the Emperor; it did not succeed and was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At Liaoyang, seeing the emperor's suffering in captivity, Empress Feng had a eunuch secretly seek poison to drink herself and offer the emperor; the attempt failed.

sentences.zh: 又行二百里，會國母為永康王所執，永康王請帝卻往遼陽城駐泊，帝遣使奉表於永康，且賀克捷，自是帝一行稍得供給。

translations.literal: After another two hundred li they met the empress dowager seized by Prince Yongkang; Prince Yongkang asked the Emperor to return and halt at Liaoyang city; the Emperor sent envoys with a memorial to Yongkang and also congratulated him on his victory; from then on the Emperor's party somewhat obtained supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li farther on they found the Khitan empress dowager held by Prince Yongkang, who asked the emperor to stay at Liaoyang; the emperor sent memorials congratulating his victory, and thereafter the party received some supplies.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐二年二月，帝自遼陽城發赴建州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Qianyou of Han, the Emperor set out from Liaoyang city for Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Han Qianyou's second year the emperor left Liaoyang for Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 行至中路，太妃安氏得疾而薨，乃焚之，載其燼骨而行。

translations.literal: Midway on the journey Grand Consort An fell ill and died; they cremated her and carried her ashes along.
translations.idiomatic: En route Grand Consort An fell ill and died; they cremated her and carried her ashes onward.

sentences.zh: 帝自遼陽行十數日，過儀州、灞州，遂至建州。

translations.literal: After the Emperor had traveled from Liaoyang for more than ten days, passing Yi Prefecture and Ba Prefecture, he then reached Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-odd days out of Liaoyang, passing Yizhou and Bazhou, he reached Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 節度使趙延暉盡禮奉迎，館帝於衙署中。

translations.literal: The military governor Zhao Yanhui received him with full ceremony and lodged the Emperor in the government office.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhao Yanhui received him with full ceremony and lodged him in the prefectural yamen.

sentences.zh: 其後割寨地五千餘頃，其地至建州數十里。

translations.literal: Thereafter they allotted more than five thousand qing of stockade land, the place being several tens of li from Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: They then allotted more than five thousand qing of frontier land a few tens of li from Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝乃令一行人員於寨地內築室分耕，給食於帝。

translations.literal: The Emperor then ordered the personnel of his party to build houses in the stockade land and divide the farming, providing food for the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had his followers build houses on the allotment, farm in common, and supply his food.

sentences.zh: 是歲，述律王子遣契丹數騎詣帝，取內人趙氏、聶氏疾馳而去。

translations.literal: That year a son of Prince Shulü sent several Khitan horsemen to the Emperor to take the inner women Zhao and Nie and gallop off with them in haste.
translations.idiomatic: That year a son of Prince Shulü sent Khitan riders to seize the inner women Zhao and Nie, the emperor's favorites, and ride off with them.

sentences.zh: 趙、聶者，帝之寵姬也，及其被奪，不勝悲憤。

translations.literal: Zhao and Nie were the Emperor's favored consorts; when they were seized he could not bear the grief and rage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and Nie were his beloved consorts; their seizure overwhelmed him with grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐三年八月，太后薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Qianyou of Han, the empress dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Han Qianyou's third year the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，有漢人自塞北而至者，言帝與後及諸子俱無恙，猶在建州，其隨從職官役使人輩，自蕃中亡歸，物故者大半矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande of Zhou, a Han man came from north of the frontier and said the Emperor, the empress, and all the sons were unharmed and still at Jian Prefecture; of the attendant officials, servants, and envoys who had fled from the Khitan lands back home, more than half had died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhou Xiande a man from beyond the frontier reported that the emperor, empress, and sons were still alive at Jianzhou; of the officials and servants who had escaped the Khitan, more than half were dead.

translations.literal: 〈Note:
translations.idiomatic: 〈Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （《郡齋讀書志》云：《晉朝陷蕃記》，範質撰。

translations.literal: (Notes on Books from the Prefect's Studio states: Record of the Jin Dynasty's Fall into the Khitan Lands, composed by Fan Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: (Notes on Books from the Prefect's Studio: Record of the Jin Dynasty's Fall into the Khitan Lands, by Fan Zhi.

sentences.zh: 質，石晉末在翰林，為出帝草降表，知其事為詳。

translations.literal: Zhi, at the end of Later Jin, was in the Hanlin Academy and drafted the surrender memorial for Emperor Chu; he knew the events in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi served in the Hanlin at the end of Jin and drafted Emperor Chu's surrender; he knew the events in detail.

sentences.zh: 記少帝初遷於黃龍府，後居於建州，凡十八年而卒。

translations.literal: The record states that the Minor Emperor was first moved to Huanglong Prefecture and later dwelt at Jian Prefecture; altogether eighteen years and then he died.
translations.idiomatic: He records that the minor emperor was first sent to Huanglong, later to Jianzhou, and died after eighteen years.

sentences.zh: 案：契丹丙午歲入汴，順數至甲子歲為十八年，實太祖乾德二年也。

translations.literal: According to the case: in the bingwu year of the Khitan they entered Bian; counting forward to the jiazi year is eighteen years—in fact the second year of Qiande of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan entered Bian in bingwu; counting forward to jiazi is eighteen years—the second year of Taizu's Qiande.

sentences.zh: 《五代史補》：少主之嗣位也，契丹以不俟命而擅立；

translations.literal: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When the Minor Lord succeeded the throne, the Khitan, because he had not awaited command but had set himself up on his own authority;
translations.idiomatic: Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties: When the minor emperor succeeded, the Khitan resented his taking the throne without leave;

sentences.zh: 又，景延廣辱其使。

translations.literal: moreover, Jing Yanguang had insulted their envoy.
translations.idiomatic: and Jing Yanguang had insulted their envoy.

sentences.zh: 契丹怒，舉國南侵。

translations.literal: The Khitan were enraged and invaded south with the whole state.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they invaded south with the whole nation.

sentences.zh: 以駙馬都尉杜重威等領駕下精兵甲禦之於中流渡橋。

translations.literal: They had the imperial son-in-law Du Chongwei and others lead the elite troops under the imperial carriage to resist them at the Zhongliu Crossing Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei the imperial son-in-law and others led the palace guard to hold them at Zhongliu Crossing.

sentences.zh: 既而契丹之眾已深入，而重威等奏報未到朝廷。

translations.literal: Soon the Khitan forces had already penetrated deeply, yet Chongwei and the others' memorial reports had not yet reached the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan were already deep in the country while Chongwei's reports had not reached court.

sentences.zh: 時桑維翰罷相，為開封府尹，謂僚佐曰：「事急矣，非大臣鉗口之時。

translations.literal: At that time Sang Weihan had left the chancellorship and was Kaifeng prefect; he told his aides: "Matters are urgent; this is no time for great ministers to keep silent."
translations.idiomatic: Sang Weihan, now out of office and prefect of Kaifeng, told his staff, "This is urgent—not a time for ministers to hold their tongues."

sentences.zh: 」乃叩內閣求見，欲請車駕親征，以固將士之心。

translations.literal: He knocked at the inner gates requesting audience, wishing to ask that the imperial carriage personally campaign to steady the soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He knocked at the inner gates, asking the emperor to take the field in person to steady the troops.

sentences.zh: 而少主方在後苑調鷹，至暮竟不召。

translations.literal: But the Minor Lord was just in the rear park training hawks and to evening was never summoned.
translations.idiomatic: But the minor emperor was in the rear park flying hawks and never summoned him before nightfall.

sentences.zh: 維翰退而嘆曰：「國家阽危如此，草澤逋客亦宜下問，況大臣求見而不召耶！

translations.literal: Weihan withdrew and sighed: "The state is in such peril on the brink; even a fugitive in the grasslands ought to be questioned—how much more when a great minister seeks audience and is not summoned!
translations.idiomatic: Weihan withdrew sighing, "The state totters on the brink—even a fugitive in the wilds should be consulted, let alone a minister who is refused audience!

sentences.zh: 事亦可知矣。

translations.literal: The outcome can already be known."
translations.idiomatic: The outcome was already plain."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，杜重威之徒降於契丹，少主遂北遷。）〉

translations.literal: Before long Du Chongwei and his party surrendered to the Khitan, and the Minor Lord then moved north.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Soon Du Chongwei surrendered and the minor emperor went north.)〉

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：少帝以中人之才，嗣將墜之業，屬上天不祐，仍歲大饑，尚或絕強敵之歡盟，鄙輔臣之謀略。

translations.literal: The historian says: The Minor Emperor, with talent of the middling sort, succeeded a falling enterprise; heaven did not favor him and famine continued year after year; he still could cut off friendly alliance with a strong enemy and despised his assisting ministers' stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: The minor emperor, a man of middling talent, inherited a failing house; heaven withheld favor and famine ran year on year; he still spurned alliance with a strong foe and scorned his ministers' counsel.

sentences.zh: 奢淫自縱，謂有泰山之安；

translations.literal: Extravagance and debauchery he indulged on his own, thinking he had the security of Mount Tai;
translations.idiomatic: He gave himself to luxury, believing he had Mount Tai's security;

sentences.zh: 委托非人，坐受平陽之辱。

translations.literal: he entrusted affairs to unfit men and sat to receive the disgrace of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: he entrusted power to the wrong men and sat to suffer Pingyang's shame.

sentences.zh: 族行萬里，身老窮荒。

translations.literal: His clan traveled ten thousand li; his person aged in the utter wilds.
translations.idiomatic: His clan marched ten thousand li; he grew old in the wilderness.

sentences.zh: 自古亡國之醜者，無如帝之甚也。

translations.literal: Of the ugly ends of lost states since antiquity, none equals the Emperor's.
translations.idiomatic: Of ruined rulers since antiquity, none was shamed as deeply.

sentences.zh: 千載之後，其如恥何，傷哉！

translations.literal: A thousand years hence, how can shame be borne—grievous indeed!
translations.idiomatic: A thousand years on, what shame can compare—how grievous!
